summary_paragraph: A male patient with a complex medical history including mitochondrial disease, atrial fibrillation, prior TIAs, dysautonomia, and coronary artery disease was admitted for acute onset vertigo and transient word-finding difficulty. Initial concern for stroke prompted a CT head and subsequent MRI/MRA of the brain and neck, all of which were negative for acute infarct, hemorrhage, or vascular abnormality. The patient reported feeling unwell for a week prior, and given the clinical course and absence of stroke findings, the symptoms were attributed to viral vestibulopathy, possibly compounded by autonomic dysfunction. His home apixaban was continued, aspirin was briefly added and then discontinued, and antihypertensives were held initially but resumed at discharge. The patient improved clinically, with resolution of vertigo and return to baseline cognition. He was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume all prior medications and follow up with his neurology and endocrinology teams.
problems: Atherosclerotic heart disease of native coronary artery without angina pectoris
